page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized instance provisioned with 16 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, it features 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core and dedicated CPU allocation. The processor architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware feature flags supporting AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA extensions. The configuration allocates 2 GB of memory per vCPU and contains no local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation highlights strong single-core CPU execution, achieving a top 25% stress-ng score of 2926.98. Memory performance is similarly strong, registering a top 25% PassMark memory score. Multi-core execution, Geekbench suite benchmarks, bzip3 decompression, and web serving throughput demonstrate average performance within the middle 50% tier. For small model artificial intelligence workloads, the instance achieves strong text generation throughput reaching 301.82 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the server offers a hardware profile configured around compute density rather than memory retention. Dedicated CPU cores provide stable execution for compilation tasks, continuous integration build pipelines, batch data processing, and web serving where local ephemeral disk storage is not required.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized cloud server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor featuring 16 vCPUs, 8 physical cores, and 32 GB of system memory. Built on x86_64 architecture with dedicated CPU resource allocation, it provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, 32 MB L3 cache, and instruction set support for AVX, AES, and cryptographic operations. Benchmark data demonstrates strong single-core CPU processing capabilities and memory performance alongside consistent multi-core metrics. The instance lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU acceleration, positioning it efficiently for compute-focused tasks such as software compilation, batch processing, CI/CD execution, and web serving.
